description: Team SystemON (Karachi) is building a web app that harmonizes 20+ years of MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data into one burning activity calendar, with a focus on crop burning and smog season in Pakistan. Team lead works in IT automation and data pipelines. Looking for teammates with Python, web dev (React or similar), GIS / remote sensing, data viz or ML skills.
summary: FireCalendar helps users explore Pakistan's seasonal fire activity from November 2000 to December 2025. MODIS and VIIRS detect fires at different spatial resolutions, so joining their raw counts can introduce a sensor-related discontinuity. We count common fire cell-days and use overlapping observations to estimate local, month-specific calibration factors on the Suomi NPP reference scale. An interactive map, monthly calendar, anomaly view and exports make the record accessible. Area-specific held-out validation and observation limitations help users interpret the reconstructed values.
details: Users select an area in Pakistan, explore monthly archived hotspots, and inspect harmonized activity, seasonal patterns and unusual months. Rectangle selection links the map to an area briefing. The application also provides a seasonal Trust Meter, descriptive before/after comparisons, and CSV/PNG exports. Each product is counted in distinct 0.01-degree fire cell-days. Local 1-degree calibration cells and calendar-month ratios relate source sensors to S-NPP. Sparse cells borrow strength from regional ratios through smoothing. The method is evaluated by leaving out an overlap year, fitting on the remaining years and comparing reconstructed values with observed S-NPP values. Validation is reported for the selected area, alongside a national-ratio baseline. Performance varies by area; local calibration is not always better. The interface is built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Leaflet. The Python API uses FastAPI, pandas and NumPy, with Parquet support through PyArrow. The repository includes the required Pakistan archive and local startup instructions. The product supports exploration and communication of seasonal fire activity. It does not estimate burned perimeter, prove policy causation, provide cloud-free coverage, or eliminate every sensor difference. Reconstruction error bands are model-error bands, not statistical confidence intervals. Use of AI tools: AI assistants were used for research/information gathering and for data analysis and interpretation.
